This is because the operation effectively reduces \( N \) modulo \( K \) with each step until it reaches the smallest non-negative residue.

thought_path_snapshot: The operation described essentially reduces the value of \( N \) by repeatedly taking the absolute difference with \( K \). The minimum value achievable is the remainder when \( N \) is divided by \( K \), because this remainder is the closest point to zero that can be reached through repeated subtractions of \( K \) or additions of \( K \) (whichever is necessary to reach the remainder). Therefore, the correct approach is to compute \( N \% K \).
Consider the relationship between N and K modulo K to understand how the operation affects the value of N.
